groups.label: Business failure
groups.reading: Staley, The Art of Short Selling; Fearon, Dead Companies Walking

groups.label: Accounting quality
groups.reading: Schilit, Financial Shenanigans; O'glove, Quality of Earnings; SEC Financial Reporting Manual

groups.label: People and control
groups.reading: Staley; McLean and Elkind, The Smartest Guys in the Room

groups.label: Tradability and instrument
groups.reading: Regulation SHO; NBER w9466, w20282, w16335, and w10659; AQR; Investor.gov leveraged-ETF bulletin

frameworks.label: Cycle / mean reversion
frameworks.question: Are peak earnings, utilization, demand, or valuation being mistaken for a durable level?
frameworks.source_note: Fearon: a cycle peak is not a dead company. Separate the two before sizing a short.

frameworks.label: Supply side
frameworks.question: Is capacity, competition, inventory, or substitution likely to outrun demand?
frameworks.source_note: Staley field cases and Fearon competitive decay.

frameworks.label: Margin contraction
frameworks.question: Are price, mix, utilization, labor, or input costs structurally compressing margins?
frameworks.source_note: Staley balance-sheet deterioration; furnace operating-failure tags.

frameworks.label: Secular obsolescence
frameworks.question: Is the product, distribution, or cost position dying, as distinct from a down cycle?
frameworks.source_note: Fearon, Dead Companies Walking. A cyclical peak uses Cycle / mean reversion instead.

frameworks.label: Fad / single product
frameworks.question: Is the equity a story tied to one product, one customer program, or one narrative?
frameworks.source_note: Staley story stocks and Fearon fads.

frameworks.label: Regulatory
frameworks.question: Can a license, rule, investigation, contract regime, or compliance burden impair the equity?
frameworks.source_note: Richard, Confidence Game, plus furnace governance/legal tags for license, investigation, and litigation.

frameworks.label: Accounting
frameworks.question: Do recognition, capitalization, reserves, non-GAAP adjustments, or working capital obscure economics?
frameworks.source_note: Parent lens. Score a child when the filing shows which game it is.

frameworks.label: Revenue recognition
frameworks.question: Is revenue recorded too soon, or recorded when cash and the customer relationship do not support it?
frameworks.source_note: Schilit earnings shenanigans; furnace tag revenue_recognition.

frameworks.label: Earnings versus cash
frameworks.question: Are reported earnings running ahead of cash from operations?
frameworks.source_note: Schilit cash-flow shenanigans; O'glove reported versus economic earnings.

frameworks.label: Working capital
frameworks.question: Are receivables or inventory growing faster than sales in a way that pulls earnings forward?
frameworks.source_note: O'glove; Staley receivable and inventory signals.

frameworks.label: Capitalization and reserves
frameworks.question: Are costs being capitalized, or reserves released, so that today's profit is borrowed from a later period?
frameworks.source_note: Schilit and O'glove. Furnace tags capitalization and reserve_release.

frameworks.label: Acquisitions and adjusted metrics
frameworks.question: Do acquisition accounting, non-GAAP add-backs, or a company-defined KPI hide the cash economics?
frameworks.source_note: Schilit acquisition accounting and key-metric shenanigans. Furnace tags non_gaap and acquisition_accounting.

frameworks.label: Reporting integrity
frameworks.question: Has the company restated, changed auditors, reported a material weakness, or filed late?
frameworks.source_note: SEC AAER and Financial Reporting Manual. Furnace tags restatement, material_weakness, auditor_change. Always human-reviewed.

frameworks.label: Cash burn
frameworks.question: Does recurring cash consumption force debt, dilution, or a strategic retreat?
frameworks.source_note: Furnace financial oxygen: going concern and cash runway.

frameworks.label: Leverage / refinancing
frameworks.question: Can debt service, covenants, or refinancing transfer value away from common equity?
frameworks.source_note: Richard, Confidence Game. Furnace tags covenant_pressure, refinancing, financing_gap.

frameworks.label: Dilution / financing
frameworks.question: Will ATMs, warrants, converts, or stock compensation impair per-share value?
frameworks.source_note: Furnace tags serial_equity_issuance and warrant_overhang.

frameworks.label: Off balance sheet
frameworks.question: Do guarantees, variable-interest entities, swaps, or earnouts move obligations off the common equity?
frameworks.source_note: McLean and Elkind; Richard credit forensics.

frameworks.label: Governance / related party
frameworks.question: Can control, incentives, or related-party transactions create an adverse payoff asymmetry?
frameworks.source_note: McLean and Elkind. Furnace tags related_party, controlling_holder, compensation, executive_exit.

frameworks.label: Promotion and insider selling
frameworks.question: Is promotional guidance meeting a rise in insider or sponsor supply of stock?
frameworks.source_note: Staley management and promotion cases. A Form 4 citation is required before this lens is scored.

frameworks.label: Fraud / bad actors
frameworks.question: Is there sourced evidence of promotion, self-dealing, misrepresentation, or enforcement risk?
frameworks.source_note: Conclusion tag only. A publisher report cannot set it. Requires a regulator, a court, an admitted restatement, or an evidence-backed analyst determination.

frameworks.label: Structural / path decay
frameworks.question: Does the security wrapper create compounding, roll, fee, swap, or tracking drag independent of the issuer?
frameworks.source_note: Investor.gov leveraged and inverse ETF bulletin. Furnace tags daily_reset, tracking_risk, swap_exposure. ECHX stays in the ls-algo book.

frameworks.label: Borrow and carry
frameworks.question: Does the borrow fee, utilization, or recall risk consume the fundamental edge?
frameworks.source_note: Regulation SHO and NBER w20282 shorting premium. A missing fee is pending, never zero.

frameworks.label: Crowding and squeeze
frameworks.question: Can days-to-cover, a crowded short, or an options squeeze force an exit before the catalyst?
frameworks.source_note: NBER w9466 and w16335. FINRA days-to-cover is context, including the biotech factor file. It is not a reason to short.

frameworks.label: Path and timing
frameworks.question: Is there a catalyst window inside the period we can afford to be early?
frameworks.source_note: Richard, Confidence Game. A right fundamental view without a catalyst stays a candidate.

frameworks.label: Issuer retaliation
frameworks.question: Is the company fighting short sellers through litigation, a squeeze, or a disclosure campaign?
frameworks.source_note: NBER w10659, Go Down Fighting. A risk flag, not a signal to press the short.

candidates.hypothesis: The thermal-barrier growth narrative may not convert into durable per-share free cash flow before competitive supply, customer concentration, and capital intensity pressure economics.
catalysts: Thermal-barrier utilization or pricing miss
Owner earnings remain negative after normalized capital spending
Customer program delay or lower EV production
falsifiers: Sustained positive free cash flow without equity issuance
Evidence of durable pricing power and diversified design wins
Capital intensity falls while margins expand

methodology.entry_price: Opened price is adjusted by the cumulative split factor so it stays comparable to the current share basis.
methodology.borrow: Borrow is supplied by the IBKR refresh feed. Unavailable is not a zero rate.
methodology.leads: An activist-index hit, an always-review filing event, or a Fugazi scorecard row creates a lead. It does not create a position and does not overwrite a rejected, live, closed, or researching row.
methodology.crowding: Days to cover is FINRA context from the biotech short-interest file when that symbol is present. It is not a reason to short.
methodology.excluded: ECHX is managed in the ls-algo universe and is omitted from this book.
